blocks.text: What an AI assistant for bookkeepers does on a Mac

An AI assistant for bookkeepers is a helper that sees what you see. Lazur runs on your Mac and lives in the notch at the top of the screen. You hold ⌥ ⌘, meaning Option and Command together, and speak. It answers out loud. It also points at the cell, row or menu you mean.

That is the core of it. You do not have to describe a spreadsheet to a chatbot or paste it into a window. Lazur reads the sheet where it sits, while you keep working in Excel or Google Sheets with the client file open.

Lazur has several modes. It explains things on screen, points at them, guides you one click at a time, and drafts or dictates text. It also runs research in its own Chrome tabs and sets reminders or calendar events. The mode you use decides what it does.

It does not click for you. It does not edit your files or run other apps on your behalf. That limit matters for bookkeeping. The books stay in your hands. Lazur works more like a colleague who looks over your shoulder and tells you what they see.
Where a bookkeeper's day goes, based on the research

The clearest public source is the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics. It lists the core duties. Bookkeepers enter financial transactions into accounting software and assign each item to the correct account. They receive and record cash, checks and vouchers. They produce balance sheets and income statements, and they check postings for accuracy.

The same BLS profile includes reconciling records and reporting the differences. It also says many of these roles need specialized accounting software, spreadsheets and databases, and comfort with computers. Most of the day runs through a few windows: the ledger, a spreadsheet, the bank portal and your inbox.

Read these numbers with care. The Zapier figure comes from a survey of small and medium business workers and owners, not bookkeepers, and the page gives no survey date. The 28 percent email figure is a 2012 McKinsey estimate about knowledge workers. The original report was not available to check, so it comes through an Alkmist article.

The labor outlook is also worth a look. BLS projects employment of these clerks to fall 6 percent from 2025 to 2035, a drop of about 85,600 jobs. Typing speed is not the skill that holds up here. Checking numbers and explaining them is.
Coding transactions and fixing postings in Excel and Google Sheets

Coding is where many errors start. Each transaction needs the right account. A wrong account can hide for weeks, until the balance sheet stops matching the bank. Checking postings is part of the job BLS names directly, so build time for it into your week.

Lazur helps in two ways here. It points at the row or column you doubt. It also explains a formula you inherited. Select the cell, hold ⌥ ⌘, and ask what the formula does. It reads the logic out loud in plain words.
Excel for Mac shortcuts that matter when you post

Microsoft's Excel keyboard shortcuts page lists the basics for Mac. ⌘C copies and ⌘V pastes. ⌘Y redoes your last undo. Microsoft lists no separate shortcut to repeat the last action, so do not expect ⌘Y to do that. Replace is ⌘⇧H. ⌘T or F4 toggles absolute references, which matters when you copy a formula down a column.

One trap: Shift+F11 inserts a new worksheet, but Microsoft marks it as possibly clashing with a macOS shortcut. If nothing happens, check System Settings > Keyboard > Keyboard Shortcuts. Then try Insert > Worksheet from the menu bar. Do not assume the feature is broken.

Google Sheets handles the same job differently. A dropdown for account codes lives under Data > Data validation. For the full steps, read [how to create a dropdown list in Google Sheets](/how-to/create-a-dropdown-list-in-google-sheets). If you would rather not hunt through menus, ask Lazur to guide you one click at a time.
Our bookkeeper pages cover both tools in more depth. See [Excel for bookkeepers](/for/bookkeepers/excel) and [Google Sheets for bookkeepers](/for/bookkeepers/google-sheets).
Bank reconciliation without the hunt for the difference

Reconciliation means matching your books to the bank statement, then explaining every gap. The hard part is rarely the total. It is the one row that moved. A deposit recorded on the wrong day, or a fee nobody entered, can cost a whole afternoon.

Start at the difference cell, not the top of the sheet. Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask Lazur where the difference is. It circles the cell and labels it. Then ask what sits directly above it. Most gaps come from timing, duplicates or a missing entry. Check those in that order.

Work in small passes. In Excel, use Data > Sort so matching amounts sit together. In Google Sheets, Data > Create a filter does the same job. Keep the bank statement open beside the sheet. Name the line you want, and Lazur points at it if it is on screen.

Duplicates need care. Excel's Data > Remove Duplicates deletes the extra rows from the sheet. Save a copy of the workbook first, with a name that shows the date. Lazur can guide you through the dialog, one click at a time, but it does not press the button. You decide which rows go.
Receipts, vouchers and data you move by hand

BLS lists receiving and recording cash, checks and vouchers as core work. Receipts arrive as photos, PDFs and forwarded emails. Each one needs a date, an amount, an account and a link to the bank line it paid.

Zapier's survey points at the big time sink: moving data from one place to another. Its respondents were general office workers, not bookkeepers. Still, the chore is familiar. You copy a total from a PDF into a sheet, then into the ledger, then into a note to a client. Each copy is a chance for a typo.

Lazur does not transfer the figures for you. It can read what is on screen and explain it. You can hold fn and dictate a short memo at the cursor. You can ask it to draft the request for a missing receipt. Those steps save the most time.

A simple habit helps. Name each receipt file with the date, the vendor and the amount when you save it. Then the sheet and the file match at a glance. When you need one, ask Lazur to point at the right row, and it circles it.
Client email and follow-ups in Gmail

Email takes a large slice of a bookkeeper's week. The 28 percent figure above is old and general, but the pattern will look familiar. A document request, a reply, a chase and a reminder each take a turn. The day is full before the reconciliation starts.

In Gmail on a Mac, ask Lazur to draft the request. Tell it the points: the missing items, the due date and the tone. It writes a short message. You read it, change it, and send it yourself. Lazur does not send anything for you.

Gmail has tools that fit this work. You can snooze a message you cannot answer today, or schedule a reply to send later. Read [how to snooze an email in Gmail](/how-to/snooze-an-email-in-gmail) and [how to schedule an email in Gmail](/how-to/schedule-an-email-to-send-later-in-gmail). For client folders, [how to create a label in Gmail](/how-to/create-a-label-in-gmail) keeps threads together.
For the chase itself, ask Lazur to set a reminder. It adds the item to Apple Reminders, or to Calendar if you want it on a specific day. The follow-up no longer lives only in your head.
Month-end reports and checking your numbers

BLS lists producing balance sheets and income statements as core work. Month-end is when one bad posting shows up in every report. Check the report totals against the ledger before you send anything to a client or an owner.

items: Open the bank statement and the sheet side by side, on one screen.
Ask Lazur to point at each line that moved a lot from last month, and to explain what it sees.
Check postings against the source documents, not against the sheet alone.
Note any open difference, and who owns the fix, in the memo field.
Save the file with the period in the name before you send it.

blocks.text: Be clear about what Lazur can and cannot know. It sees the screen. It does not know why a number moved. Treat its explanation as a lead, then confirm it against the source document. That habit catches the errors that matter.

For a chart in a client update, see [how to make a chart in Google Sheets](/how-to/make-a-chart-in-google-sheets). For consistent vendor names, use [find and replace in Google Sheets](/how-to/find-and-replace-text-in-google-sheets).
Client data, your employer's rules and what Lazur sends

Bookkeepers handle bank details, payroll and tax numbers. Follow your firm's rules on client data before you show any of it to an AI tool. If your employer has a policy on AI tools, read it first. If you work for yourself, your client agreements set the limits.

blocks.title: Check the rules before live files
blocks.text: Lazur sends audio and screenshots to AI providers to answer your question. Check your employer's rules on client data before you use it on live client files.

Here is what Lazur does with what it sees. It listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer you. They are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. These are product facts, not a compliance certificate, and they do not replace your own rules.

Some habits lower the risk. Close tabs that show full account numbers before you hold the shortcut. Hide columns with tax IDs. Ask about the transaction and its account, not about the person behind it.
Common mistakes with an AI assistant for bookkeeping

The first mistake is trusting a guess. An AI assistant reads what is on screen. It does not see your bank feed, your audit trail or the email from a client last week. If the answer depends on something off screen, open that thing and show it.
The second mistake is asking for the whole job at once. Ask for one step. Point first, then explain, then guide. Small questions get checked answers faster, and you catch a wrong turn early.

The third mistake is skipping the version check. Menus change between releases. Intuit's update page lists two QuickBooks Desktop for Mac releases, Mac Plus 2024 R13 and Mac Plus 2023 R7.6, and does not say which is newest. Open the app's Help menu and check your version before you follow any menu path from a guide, including ours.
The fourth mistake is dictating into the wrong field. Dictation types at the cursor. Click into the memo field first, then hold fn and speak. Read the text back before you save.

Lazur pricing, the free trial and how to start

Lazur has a three-day Pro trial with no credit card. The trial starts the first time you open the app. Pro costs $18 a month, or $15 a month billed annually, and includes 250 AI actions. Power costs $120 a month, or $96 a month billed annually, and includes 1,000 AI actions. Dictation is unlimited on both.

Compare those numbers with your own time. If the assistant saves you a lost afternoon in a month, the math is easy. If it saves only a few minutes a week, Pro may already be more than you need. Check the [pricing page](/pricing) for current terms before you decide.
To start, [download Lazur for Mac](/download). It runs on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, not available.
Your first hour with Lazur on real books

Start with a file you already know. Open last month's reconciliation. Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask where the difference is. Then ask what sits above it. A few minutes of this teaches the rhythm faster than reading ever will.
Next, dictate one memo. Click into a field, hold fn, speak and release. Check the text before you save it. Last, ask Lazur to draft one client request. Read it aloud before you send it.

If your books live in Google Sheets, the [Google Sheets page for bookkeepers](/for/bookkeepers/google-sheets) covers reconciliation and limits in more detail. Excel users can start with [Excel for bookkeepers](/for/bookkeepers/excel).

faq.question: Can an AI assistant for bookkeepers see my whole bank account?
faq.answer: No. Lazur only sees what is on your screen, and it only listens and looks while you hold the shortcut. If the bank portal is not open, Lazur cannot see it. Open the page you need, one screen at a time.

faq.question: Does Lazur work inside QuickBooks, Xero or other accounting software?
faq.answer: It works with whatever is on your Mac screen, but it is not a plugin or add-in for any app. Lazur has no partnership with any app maker. Check your app version first, because menus change between releases.

faq.question: Is Lazur safe to use with client financial data?
faq.answer: Lazur does not certify anything about client data, and this page does not claim any compliance certification. Audio and screenshots go to AI providers to answer your question. They are not stored, and content is never used to train AI models. Follow your employer's rules first.

faq.question: Will Lazur reconcile my accounts or post entries for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur points at rows, explains formulas and walks you through steps. It does not click buttons or edit your files. You make every entry and every decision.

faq.question: What does the free trial include?
faq.answer: The trial is three days on Pro, with no credit card. It starts the first time you open the app. Pro costs $18 a month, or $15 a month billed annually, and includes 250 AI actions. Dictation is unlimited on both plans.

faq.question: Does Lazur work on Windows?
faq.answer: Not yet. Lazur is a Mac app for Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, but it is not available.

faq.question: Does Lazur remember my earlier questions?
faq.answer: Yes. Lazur keeps a memory of what you asked and did, and that memory stays on the Mac. It helps you pick up a reconciliation where you left off.

faq.question: Can I use it in Excel and Google Sheets at the same time?
faq.answer: Yes. It works with any app you have open on the Mac. The pages for [Excel](/for/bookkeepers/excel) and [Google Sheets](/for/bookkeepers/google-sheets) cover each one in more depth.

painPoints.title: Every line needs the right account
painPoints.text: BLS lists assigning each transaction to the correct account as a core duty. One miscoded line can send you back through weeks of postings to find it.

painPoints.title: The hunt for one missing row
painPoints.text: BLS lists reconciling records and reporting differences as core work. The total is rarely the problem. The cause is usually one row that moved or never got entered.

painPoints.title: Email on top of the numbers

painPoints.title: Receipts that arrive in pieces
